documents.evidenceText: DATES. This final rule is effective on January 11, 2021. Applicability dates for particular requirements are stated separately in the supplementary information. This final rule applies to group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual health insurance coverage. Group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual health insurance coverage must disclose cost-sharing information for a covered item or service upon request. Plans and issuers must make public machine-readable files containing in-network rates, historical out-of-network allowed amounts and billed charges, and negotiated rates and historical net prices for prescription drugs. This consumer shopping explanation applies to participants, beneficiaries, and enrollees seeking price information.

documents.evidenceText: Article 3. This Regulation applies to the processing of personal data in the context of the activities of an establishment of a controller or a processor in the Union. This Regulation also applies to processing related to offering goods or services to data subjects in the Union or monitoring their behaviour in the Union. Article 30. Each controller and, where applicable, the controller's representative, shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility. The obligations shall not apply to an enterprise or organisation employing fewer than 250 persons unless the processing is likely to result in a risk, is not occasional, or includes special categories of data or criminal-conviction data. Article 83. Infringements of specified obligations shall be subject to administrative fines up to €10,000,000 or 2 percent of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. Infringements of the basic principles and data-subject rights shall be subject to administrative fines up to €20,000,000 or 4 percent of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher. Article 99. This Regulation shall apply from 25 May 2018.

documents.versionLabel: Modern Slavery Act 2015 section 54 as enacted
documents.evidenceText: Section 54. A commercial organisation must prepare a slavery and human trafficking statement for each financial year. The term commercial organisation means a body corporate or partnership which carries on a business, or part of a business, in any part of the United Kingdom, supplies goods or services, and has a total turnover of not less than the amount prescribed. The statement must be approved by the board of directors and signed by a director. If the organisation has a website, it must publish the statement on that website and include a prominent link to it on the homepage.
